title: Game Mathematics Part 2: Rotation Interpolation 1 — Paths and Timing Between Orientations

scenes.title: 앞 편의 회전값에서 중간 자세로
lines: The previous episode found the rotation difference from the starting to the target orientation. We now construct intermediate orientations along that rotation.

scenes.title: 이번 강의에서 배울 것
lines: How do we construct natural intermediate orientations between two poses?
We will observe driving and flight, then visualize the short path and speed of quaternion interpolation.
Next, we will convert Euler angles, axis-angle, quaternions and matrices under one convention.
Finally, we will calculate the midpoint of a ninety-degree turn and verify a conversion round trip.

scenes.title: 차체와 카메라의 회전 경로 관찰
lines: This is driving on a bend in Forza Horizon4. Read the car facing separately from the following camera.
Matching the first and last directions does not prevent an awkward sudden turn between them.
Compare the front of the car, the bend and the moving background.
The footage does not reveal which interpolation function the game uses. It shows why intermediate orientations matter.
Changes in apparent car size also involve camera and distance. Following its facing separately helps avoid mixing translation with rotation.
Our next diagram will hold position and camera fixed and change only orientation.

scenes.title: 두 끝점만으로는 중간 화면이 비어 있습니다
lines: After observing the body changing direction, can we make intermediate poses by mixing the four numbers at the start and end?

scenes.title: 숫자를 섞는 것과 회전을 잇는 것
lines: Consider the midpoint between identity and a180-degree turn about z.
Averaging the entries yields a diagonal of0,0,1. Two axes collapse.
Quaternions must maintain unit length too. A component blend generally leaves the unit surface.
We will distinguish a normalized linear blend from following an arc on the unit sphere.
Matrices can be interpolated with methods that respect the rotation structure; naive entry blending is the problem.

scenes.title: 부호부터 골라 짧은 경로 만들기
lines: As we learned, q and minus q represent the same orientation, yet a component path between them can differ.
Take the dot product of unit endpoints. If it is negative, flip every component of the end quaternion.
This selects the closer representative of the same endpoint; it is not conjugation.
For endpoints q and minus q, sign alignment makes them identical, avoiding a zero midpoint.
A physical180-degree separation has two equally short paths. Choose a direction with an explicit policy.

We can also use the relative rotation from the previous lesson. After sign alignment, delta is the end quaternion times the inverse of the start. Applying delta to the power t to the start follows the same short arc.

scenes.title: 티는 회전 차이 중 얼마나 적용할지입니다
lines: In delta to the power t, t is the exponent on delta; the expression does not square t.
With a z ninety-degree delta and t equal to one half, apply half the difference, forty-five degrees, to the starting orientation.
We will now calculate weights that keep the intermediate orientation on the unit arc.

scenes.title: 절반 자세는 움직임 중간에 있습니다
lines: Observe connected poses in Skate 3. Red follows the body direction.
Blue follows the visible board length. Follow takeoff, the airborne pose and landing separately.
The fraction for constructing intermediate poses is t. The previous forty-five degrees was a worked example, not an angle measured here.

scenes.title: 가까운 방향과 돌아가는 과정
lines: Track the car facing as it follows the next bend.
An endpoint image alone does not tell whether the turn was short or included an extra revolution.
Interpolation between two orientations chooses a path without storing the number of earlier revolutions.
Interpolating a position along the road differs from interpolating orientation.
Even when two moments have similar facing, the intervening turn requires observing the motion. Distinguish endpoint orientation from rotation history over time.
Now we will relate an arc on the unit sphere to the orientation change.

scenes.title: 내적과 아크코사인이 호의 각도를 찾는 이유
lines: Following an arc requires the angle between its endpoints. Begin with the familiar unit circle in a plane.
The rightward unit vector is one, zero. A thirty-degree vector is square root three over two, one half. Multiplying corresponding entries and adding gives square root three over two.
That number is cosine of thirty degrees. Arccosine performs the reverse lookup and returns thirty degrees.
For quaternions, the dot sums four component products and gives the angle alpha in the section joining the two unit points. Alpha must be distinguished from the object's physical rotation.

scenes.title: SLERP는 단위 구면의 호를 따라갑니다
lines: Unit quaternions lie on a sphere in four dimensions, with squared components summing to one.
This circle illustrates the relevant arc in a two-dimensional section, rather than depicting the full four-dimensional sphere.
Let d be the sign-aligned dot product, and let alpha be its arccosine.
The quaternion arc angle differs from the physical turn angle: the minimum physical rotation is twice alpha.
Sine-ratio weights combine the endpoints into the point at fraction t of the arc.
This is spherical linear interpolation. It does not mean the components change linearly.

scenes.title: 움직이는 몸체와 단위 방향의 길이
lines: Red follows the body; blue follows the board direction.
Their directions change in the air before another landing.
Unit length in the calculation is a condition on the stored direction values.
It does not set the game travel distance or the displayed line length to one.

scenes.title: 맞는 식에도 입력 검사가 필요한 이유
lines: We found the unit arc, but its denominator becomes small as the endpoints coincide. Handle nearly identical orientations first.

scenes.title: 작은 각도와 잘못된 입력을 먼저 처리
lines: Our code requires finite t between zero and one. Validate and normalize both quaternion endpoints first.
Near-zero or nonfinite inputs need an error or an explicit fallback to a valid orientation.
Flip the endpoint when the dot is negative, then clamp the dot to protect arccosine from rounding error.
When d exceeds0.9995, this example uses normalized linear interpolation to avoid a small sine denominator.
Otherwise, use the sine weights and normalize the result. Check the endpoint orientations at t zero and one.

scenes.title: 주행에서는 중간 상태도 보여야 합니다
lines: In these other driving intervals, separate car facing from background motion.
The edit between excerpts is not a computed intermediate pose. Observe continuous motion within each excerpt.
Code produces intermediate rotations by changing t between the endpoints.
Imagine both a forward line and an up line on the car. A single direction can miss its twist.
A cut can change location and camera. Observe continuous pose changes within each excerpt before connecting them to the next fixed-condition calculation.
The next calculation holds camera and position fixed. For a ninety-degree turn, examine t equal to zero point two five and zero point five.

scenes.title: 관찰한 중간 자세를 작은 계산으로
lines: To verify the observation made with a moving camera, fix the camera and z axis and compute the intermediate poses of a ninety-degree turn.

scenes.title: 구십 도 회전의 중간을 직접 계산
lines: Start at[1,0,0,0], ending at a z90-degree turn:[cos45degrees,0,0,sin45degrees].
The dot is square root two over two: alpha is45degrees, while the physical rotation is90degrees.
At t equal to zero point two five, the object rotates twenty-two point five degrees, the first of four equal steps. At the halfway value t equal to zero point five, it rotates forty-five degrees.
At the third step, t equal to zero point seven five, it is sixty-seven point five degrees. Equal t intervals give equal rotation-angle intervals.
Each quaternion is converted to a matrix to draw the body axes. We can verify intermediate results as well as endpoints.

scenes.title: NLERP도 회전이지만 속도는 다릅니다
lines: NLERP aligns signs, blends components linearly and normalizes: a simple calculation that preserves unit length.
Linear progression of t generally does not produce constant physical angular speed.
Between identity and a120-degree turn, NLERP at one quarter rotates approximately27.8degrees.
SLERP gives30degrees there. Both give60degrees halfway, but differ at other points along the path.
Small differences may be hard to see. Compare motion requirements and cost without assuming SLERP is always faster.

scenes.title: 방향의 변화와 지나가는 속도 나누기
lines: Watch the order in which the red body line and blue board line change.
Travel distance and the fraction between orientations are different values. The camera also follows the action.
Fast-looking screen motion does not establish constant angular speed. We will state the timing conditions separately in the calculation.

scenes.title: 속도와 자세를 같은 값으로 읽지 않기
lines: Driving speed and angular speed are separate quantities.
Observe distance travelled and change in car facing separately.
The camera also moves, so this footage is not a measurement of exact angular velocity.
The speedometer reports travel speed, not the angular velocity of orientation. Keep units and measured quantities distinct.
A large camera turn does not imply the same car rotation. Observe car and road together to separate pose changes.
Our fixed-axis calculation can compare turn angles over equal time intervals. Changing the time function changes the speed.

scenes.title: 자세의 비율과 실제 시간을 연결하기
lines: Using intermediate orientations in playback also requires deciding how t increases over time.

scenes.title: 일정 속도에는 시간 조건도 필요합니다
lines: Constant angular speed requires fixed endpoints and t that is linear in time.
An easing function follows the same arc with a varying speed.
Repeatedly interpolating from the current pose toward a target differs from one fixed-endpoint interpolation.
A fixed fraction per frame may yield different responses at different frame rates. Design the fraction using elapsed time.
Moving-target tracking and long animation curves require their own design; a single SLERP does not solve everything.

scenes.title: 같은 호도 시간에 따라 다르게 움직입니다
lines: After the time conditions, compare the same rotation with small numbers. This defined example fixes the camera and z axis and turns from zero to ninety degrees over one second.
At half a second, elapsed time divided by duration gives t equal to one half. With linear time, half of ninety degrees is forty-five degrees.
Now use the square of the elapsed-time fraction as t. One half squared is one quarter, so the same instant gives one quarter of ninety degrees: twenty-two point five degrees.

At one second both reach t equal to one and ninety degrees. The endpoints and arc stay the same, but progress at intermediate times differs. Choosing the path and mapping time to progress are separate decisions.

scenes.title: 한 바퀴의 기록이 끝 자세에 남을까요
lines: Even after choosing a timing rule, we must check whether the final orientation retains the record of an extra complete turn.

scenes.title: 연속 부호와 여러 바퀴의 기록
lines: Making w positive independently each frame can create a component sign jump at the180-degree boundary.
Flipping a new quaternion when its dot with the previous one is negative can maintain a nearby representative.
That choice helps component continuity, but does not recover the number of revolutions.
If an animation intentionally spins a full turn, preserve intermediate keys or accumulated turn information.
The desired direction at180degrees is a design policy: shortest alone does not make the choice unique.

scenes.title: 지나온 회전의 기록과 현재 자세 나누기
lines: The red body direction changes and becomes upright again.
The current pose and the rotation history are different information.
This is a different excerpt. Follow the blue board direction separately as well.
Passing the final orientation does not also store how many turns occurred.

scenes.title: 윙슈트와 스키의 몸체 기준
lines: This is wingsuit flight down a mountain in Riders Republic. Observe the bank of the arms and body.
Position continues changing while facing and up directions change too. One facing arrow does not capture the whole orientation.
Storing the arrival orientation does not preserve every rotation made along the flight.
Separate the following camera motion too. This footage does not expose internal quaternion or interpolation code.
With different equipment too, distinguish torso facing from body bank. Attached forward and up directions provide a frame for reading orientation.
Do not connect cuts or rewind screens into continuous motion. We selected actual action within separate excerpts; imagine the three attached axes in each.
We will now choose a suitable representation for each task and convert between them.

scenes.title: 중간 자세를 다음 작업에 넘기려면
lines: We now have an intermediate orientation at one instant. Editing its angles and applying it to many vertices call for different representations.
Keep the same body axes while passing that orientation between editable angles, interpolation quaternions and matrices that transform vectors.

scenes.title: 하나만 고집하지 말고 작업에 맞게 쓰세요
lines: Euler angles suit human reading and editing, with order, equivalent encodings and singular poses to handle.
Quaternions suit composition and interpolation, but need unit-length and sign management and are hard to edit directly.
Matrices expose the three axes and suit transforming many vectors. Check orthonormality and determinant.
Float32 components alone occupy12bytes for Euler,16for a quaternion and36for a3-by-3matrix, excluding padding and metadata.
Axis-angle explains a single turn clearly. Measure compression and runtime in your implementation; other representations also have rotation-aware interpolation methods.
Storage or transmission may compress components. Reconstructing an omitted component from unit length requires sign rules and quantization-error checks. Sixteen bytes is not a universal minimum.

scenes.title: 보간한 자세를 다음 계산에 넘기기
lines: Between two orientations, we chose a path, kept unit length and specified how t follows physical time. Extra turn history needed separate storage.
We now pass one intermediate orientation to the next task. The next episode retains the same object and axes while converting angles, quaternions and matrices and verifying the same rotation.
